standards.facet: Identify flat and solid shapes across orientations
Identify flat and solid shapes across orientations
Identify flat and solid shapes across orientations

beats.say: Here is a toy block, and a square drawn beside it.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The block has a square on it. Are they both flat?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The square is flat. It goes across and up, with no thickness.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Look past the block's front. It also goes back.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: That front-to-back room is called depth. A shape with depth is solid.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.meaning: A shape with depth. It takes up room.

beats.say: One flat part doesn't make the whole block flat.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The whole block is solid. Look at the whole shape.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Which shapes could lie flat on the page? Choose three shapes.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Which shapes could lie flat on the page? Choose 3 shapes.

beats.say: Here, that means choose the flat shapes. Check each letter.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: A is a tilted rectangle. Tilting it adds no thickness, so choose A.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: B is flat too. Coloring a square doesn't give it depth.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: C is a circle, like the ring you draw around a cup.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: D looks round too. Is that another flat circle?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: D pictures a ball you could toss. Its surface curves around to the back.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: These dashes show the hidden part of a line around the ball.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: So C is flat, but D is solid. Round doesn't mean flat.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Choose A, B, and C. That is three flat shapes.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Which shapes are solid? Choose two shapes.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Which shapes are solid? Choose 2 shapes.

beats.say: A is a drawn triangle. B has the shape of a party hat.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: C has the shape of a can. D is a drawn rectangle.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: B comes to a point, but its bottom goes around. It has depth.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: C has a flat top. What about the whole can?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Look below the top. The whole can takes up room, so choose C too.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: A and D have no thickness. Leave those flat shapes unchosen.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: B and C. Two solid shapes.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Listen for flat or solid.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Check each whole shape. Flat has no thickness; solid has depth.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Check the whole shape for depth.

beats.say: Choose every match.
beats.speaker: teacher

scene.title: 4 shapes in boxes labeled A to D
scene.note: A: an outline with 4 sides, 2 long and 2 short. B: an outline with 4 sides of the same length. C: a round outline. D: a shaded ball with a dashed line around its back.
